content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Use synthetic data, keep credentials out of source/logs, and write down the verification and rollback steps. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: This checks non-empty path strings, not file existence; a production workflow also needs permissions, provenance, monitoring and rollback. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For maintaining production r workflows, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming external services always return valid data.
common_mistakes.why: Timeouts, authorization failures, rate limits and schema changes are normal failure cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Add timeouts, status/schema validation, least-privilege access and bounded retries.

common_mistakes.problem: Embedding credentials or sensitive rows in examples or logs.
common_mistakes.why: Secrets and private data can leak through source control or diagnostic output.
common_mistakes.fix: Use environment-based secret handling and synthetic examples; redact logs.

common_mistakes.problem: Leaving resources open after an error.
common_mistakes.why: Unclosed connections and files can leak resources or lock outputs.
common_mistakes.fix: Use reliable cleanup patterns and test both success and failure paths.
